8	---
9	
10	# Common Practice foundation review
11	
12	Use Common Practice's application structure and ordinary development workflow.
13	Prioritise the Cloudflare Website and API, remove every Alchemy patch, and remove
14	TaxKit's separate receipt and approval machinery. Keep Bun as a supported,
15	secondary host over the same calculation packages.
16	
17	```text
18	Website first HTML -> server runner -> native HttpApiClient -> private API binding
19	Website navigation -> shared registry -> native AtomHttpApi client -> public API
20	Public GET/HEAD -> version-scoped native Cloudflare cache (eligible responses only)
21	Local Website setup -> encoded root settings -> retained browser configuration
22	Checked API operations ---------------------------------> calculations -> rules/core
23	Machine HTTP/RPC/MCP -----------------------------> API -> calculations -> rules/core
24	Local SDK ----------------------------------------------> calculations -> rules/core
25	
26	Native API declaration -> Website declaration
27	                    API address + private binding -> Website
28	No reverse Website address dependency; publication links use Production
29	Git commit/PR -> ordinary checks -> native Alchemy -> deployed Website/API
30	                               Doppler supplies stage-specific secrets
31	```
32	
33	The comparison uses TaxKit commit `f899c963f463d2283517e908febcfa3ebb1dd442`
34	and current Common Practice main `6dc08581d1ad79b06853fe3721a5e6124d2989a1`.
35	Commonplace `development-workflows` 0.7.1 is published and installed, verified
36	against its [published release](https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins/releases/tag/%40commonplace/development-workflows%400.7.1)
37	on 13 October 2026. Its native HTTP/Atom and caching guidance supersedes the
38	11 October RPC loading proposal and copied client-service approach. Earlier
39	Common Practice comparisons remain research history, not the proposed target.
40	This document and its [plan](../exec-plans/active/common-practice-foundation-review.md)
41	replace the large, uncommitted audit packet created during this review.
42	
43	This remains the agreed research and design stage. Application code, dependency
44	versions, hosted workflows, provider resources and credentials have not changed.
45	The latest instructions determine the proposed direction; they do not require a
46	new JSON acceptance record for each finding. Common Practice is read-only.
47	
48	## Agreed direction
49	
50	| Choice | Direction |
51	| --- | --- |
52	| Website calls | Updated proposal: native HTTP clients use the private same-stage binding for server rendering and the public API directly in the browser. Use existing GET reads and calculation POSTs; native AtomHttpApi shares the browser factory/registry. Remove copied client services, loader request atoms and generated Website server functions. Existing machine RPC stays supported. |
53	| Hosts | Cloudflare first. Keep Bun and Cloudflare, with shared packages independent of either. Preserve Bun's current HTTP coverage; adding RPC/MCP to Bun is outside this change. |
54	| Alchemy | Zero Alchemy patches, including replacement monkeypatches, copied planner code or a custom provider carrying the same fixes. Redesign the declarations that currently need them. |
55	| Public HTTP helpers | Q5 agreed replacement of generic-callback and callable Layer helpers. Native generated endpoint clients already provide named checked operations: use them directly, with static host composition, rather than copying methods into another service. Update callers/examples and normal package versioning together. |
56	| Browser access and publication links | Q6 agreed Common Practice's public, credential-free browser API policy and Production canonical/publication links on 13 October. Keep actual API endpoint addresses stage-specific and each host's own native URL. |
57	| Public response caching | Q7 agreed seven-day Cloudflare freshness on 13 October for eligible public documentation and fixed metadata. Browsers recheck; cache storage is version-scoped. Personal calculation inputs/results, sessions, errors and Set-Cookie responses remain uncached. |
58	| External MCP tools | Q8 agreed native Effect: allow Origin-less desktop/server clients and listed browser sites. Initially list `https://taxkit.dev`; add other sites only for a known need. No Effect predicate patch or Preview Website address dependency. TaxKit's on-page tools remain independent. |
59	| Browser loader freshness | Q9 agreed one-minute reuse of public documentation/metadata through native TanStack settings. Personal submission/results and live local configuration remain outside that public reuse policy. |
60	| Development and operations | Ordinary commits, pull requests, checks, GitHub Actions, native Alchemy and native Doppler, following Common Practice. Remove receipt packets, duplicated approval records and checks whose only purpose is to verify that paperwork. |
61	| Operational information | Allow fixed safe details such as app, stage, route category, duration and safe failure category. Exclude salaries, facts, results, calculation traces, raw URLs, request bodies and raw errors. PostHog remains postponed. |
62	
63	The host and privacy choices are also recorded in [ADR 0003](../adr/0003-support-independent-api-hosts.md)
64	and [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-limit-operational-observations.md). The earlier
65	[shared Axiom dataset choice](../adr/0002-reuse-shared-telemetry-datasets.md)
66	remains: reference the existing three physical datasets, with TaxKit-owned scoped
67	access and destinations. The public access/link choice is recorded in
68	[ADR 0005](../adr/0005-public-api-and-production-publication-links.md).
69	No collection is enabled by this review.
70	
71	## What to copy from Common Practice
72	
73	| Area | Common Practice source | TaxKit adoption |
74	| --- | --- | --- |
75	| Server execution | `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts` | One frontend server runtime, constructed in the application. Services and tax packages never start their own runtime. |
76	| Browser state | `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts`, `router.tsx`, `routes/__root.tsx` | One application runtime factory and browser registry, created before loaders and shared with React. Native AtomHttpApi uses that factory. Keep form commands, retained configuration and cancellation. |
77	| Website loaders | `apps/web/src/lib/seo/page.loader.ts` | Local server/browser branches call native clients through one required host bridge. TanStack owns results and freshness; local settings need no Website data endpoint. |
78	| Native clients | `packages/http/src/api.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts`, `runtime.client.ts` | Native HttpApi contracts and generated clients own encoding, decoding and declared errors. Keep adapters only for real tax/workflow policy or checked host conversion. No replica client service. |
79	| Native caching | `apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts`, Website `build/cloudflare.ts`, `packages/http/src/publishing.policy.ts` | Native version-scoped cache declarations and a small public-response/header policy. No global Cache API wrapper or custom cache runtime. |
80	| Private Cloudflare calls | `apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts` | Put Cloudflare binding conversion in one Website-owned adapter. Use native Alchemy conversion where it preserves caller trust and complete reply handling. |
81	| Resource declarations | `alchemy.run.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/build/cloudflare.ts`, `apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts` | Declare the API before the Website. Website uses the API's actual address and private binding. Keep deployment code at the app/infrastructure owners. |
82	| Secrets | `packages/infrastructure/src/secrets.ts` | One native source list: Doppler, ignored `.env` overrides, disabled shell-value fallback. Keep TaxKit's own project, configs and credentials. |
83	| Commands | Root `package.json` | Short commands calling native Alchemy directly. Keep one understandable verification command. |
84	| Automation | `.github/workflows/checks.yml`, `preview.yml`, `production.yml` | Checks on PR/main; PR previews and close-event cleanup; manual main-only Production. Native dry-run/deploy, small public smoke checks and native Production drift. |
85	| Everyday records | Git commits, PRs, workflow logs and Alchemy state | Use these ordinary records. No additional repository receipt files or approval-envelope system. |
86	
87	These are paths within Common Practice, not personal checkout paths. Reuse the
88	approach and required code, not its project names, access tokens or provider IDs.
89	
90	Common Practice still runs build, formatting, lint, types, Effect checks, tests,
91	unused-code and documentation checks. Its workflow does not support a claim that
92	all verification disappears. TaxKit should remove checks of ceremony while
93	keeping tests that catch wrong tax answers, broken public contracts or a broken
94	Website/API.
95	
96	## Complete calls and the HTTP/RPC comparison
97	
98	A host is the environment running the API, such as Cloudflare or Bun. HTTP, RPC
99	and MCP are different ways to send a request to that same API. The local SDK is
100	a library that calculates inside the caller's program.
101	
102	| Call | Current path and behaviour to preserve |
103	| --- | --- |
104	| Browser calculation | Page container -> existing Atom command -> native public HTTP calculation POST -> API handler -> `PublicCalculatorService` -> catalogue/fact checks -> Australian rules/Core -> checked report -> the same Atom state and rendering leaf. Editing or leaving the page cancels pending browser work. |
105	| Server HTML form | Website checks the 64 KiB POST -> native HTTP client -> trusted private API method carrying the checked original caller identity separately from JSON -> the same calculation service -> checked submission data. Keep working without JavaScript. |
106	| Machine HTTP | HTTP declarations decode requests with the owning Schemas -> handler -> the same calculation service -> existing status/error envelope. Native generated clients use these declarations directly, without a copied method service. |
107	| Machine RPC | Revision-four checked operations -> the same service. Keep the current encoded replies and safe named failures. |
108	| Remote MCP | API tool definitions reuse the owning Schemas and shared service. Keep current request/cancellation ownership and Cloudflare session support. |
109	| Local SDK | Checked in-process request -> the same calculation service. Effect callers own their services; the Promise-facing SDK privately owns its necessary runtime and closes it. It does not become a network SDK. |
110	
111	| Comparison | Common Practice | TaxKit decision |
112	| --- | --- | --- |
113	| Website transport | Public reads now use native HTTP GET/HEAD contracts; SSR uses the private binding and browser calls the API directly. Owned publishing RPC and copied client wrappers are removed there. | Use TaxKit's existing HTTP contract for docs/catalogue/metadata and calculation POSTs. Keep machine RPC/MCP contracts; removing them is not part of copying Website loading. |
114	| Named operations | Native generated endpoint methods already check declared inputs, replies and errors. | Call those methods directly. Keep only real input/report correlation, bounded transport and feature error policy; do not add a replica Content or CalculatorAccess client service. |
115	| Errors and serialisation | Typed errors are handled once at the page/tool/HTTP boundary; native TanStack serialises successful views. | Preserve existing HTTP status/error envelopes and RPC errors. Retire Website-only success/error envelopes and repeat reply decoding; retain owning domain Schemas and necessary view conversion. |
116	| Original caller identity | Ordinary public content reads need no anonymous-calculation admission policy. | Keep the trusted private calculation capability. Extend its exact POST admission from `/rpc` to the canonical HTTP calculation path without accepting caller keys from JSON or forwarded headers. |
117	| Cancellation and bounds | A shared native client remains available while each loader call receives its own AbortSignal. | Retain request cancellation, ten-second complete-call budget, 2 MiB response cap and no automatic operation retries. The trusted private method still cannot transmit a remote AbortSignal; its five-second work budget remains. |
118	| Response variants | One checked helper relates a selected page format to the native decoded response. | TaxKit's current docs page and Markdown are separate endpoints; do not invent a format wrapper. Keep calculation ID/report-kind and other genuine request/reply checks. |
119	| Package consumers | Common Practice is private/source-oriented. | Preserve TaxKit's compiled exports, public HTTP/RPC/MCP contracts and packed SDK consumers. Q5 helper signatures change through normal Changesets; native client exposure is not an unchecked SDK escape hatch. |
120	
121	The updated transport recommendation follows the new full comparison. Q6 now
122	selects public credential-free HTTP/RPC browser access for valid HTTP(S) origins
123	and fixed Production publication links. Admit actual native CORS headers, retain
124	caller/rate/body/work policies, and keep each stage's API endpoint addresses.
125	Q8 separately selects native MCP origin admission; WebMCP registration stays
126	bound to the actual Website host.
127	
128	## Native HTTP loader and client migration
129	
130	TaxKit installs Effect/Atom React 4.0.0, patched Alchemy beta.80, TanStack Start
131	1.168.60 and Router 1.170.41. Common Practice qualifies its implementation at
132	Effect 4.0.2 and unpatched Alchemy beta.81. Installed source already supplies
133	AtomHttpApi.Service's runtime-factory option and the relevant native client APIs.
134	Matching upstream clones inform the design; neither this comparison nor the
135	published plugin authorises an upgrade.
136	
137	| Website need | Native TaxKit owner and migration |
138	| --- | --- |
139	| Calculator catalogue/metadata | Existing `TaxKitApi.calculatorApi` GET endpoints and owning Schemas. Root catalogue remains domain data, distinct from local settings. |
140	| Docs page/navigation/search | Existing `TaxKitApi.content` GET endpoints with checked path/query inputs. Preserve accepted-only content, full page/metadata before rendering, Unicode/empty search behaviour and MDX presentation. |
141	| Markdown | Existing checked text endpoint. Reuse API-owned finished responses/negotiation where possible; keep correct media type, status and GET/HEAD behaviour. |
142	| Discovery files | No current HTTP endpoint. Add narrow native API GET/HEAD handlers for the existing checked discovery paths, reuse the existing formatter and bounded document Schema, and forward the finished reply through one Website binding request. Keep the machine RPC operation unchanged; add no second renderer or browser API proxy. |
143	| Calculation | Existing native POST `/api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/calculate`. Keep calculator-specific input decoding, explicit submit, returned ID/report-kind checks and stale-answer/interruption rules. Calculation data remains uncached. |
144	| Root configuration | Local checked Website settings and any Website-owned cookie. Keep invalid-setting recovery and retained configuration; do not add a settings API call. |
145	
146	`loaders.ts` uses local `createIsomorphicFn` branches and matching runtime import
147	owners. Remove settings/page/search `createServerFn` wrappers, generated path
148	allowlists and loader headers together. The server uses one `runtime` and a
149	static Layer holding `HttpApiClient.make(TaxKitApi)` over Alchemy's public
150	`fromCloudflareFetcher`/`toHttpClient` conversion. A native client value may have
151	a host-owned service tag for acquisition; it must not be a copied method map.
152	Keep selected checked Config and the original binding receiver. Calculation
153	uses the existing trusted `calculatorRequest` capability after its exact route
154	admission is extended; ordinary binding fetch cannot supply caller identity.
155	
156	Move the existing browser composition to `runtime.client.ts`. Declare the native
157	`ApiClient` with `AtomHttpApi.Service`, `runtime: browserRuntime.factory` and the
158	existing FetchHttpClient Layer. Use a checked baseUrl or native `httpClient(get)`
159	configuration hook. Confirm that credentials/redirect settings reach execution
160	in installed 4.0.0; do not assume the qualified 4.0.2 Layer's context handling.
161	Keep checked configuration atoms alive and local optional services independent.
162	
163	Create one registry in `createLoaderRegistry` before router loaders run. React
164	uses that exact registry through `RegistryContext.Provider`; SSR uses an isolated
165	RegistryProvider. Declare the retained native runtime atom once, for example
166	`const apiClientRuntime = ApiClient.runtime.pipe(Atom.keepAlive)`, then read it
167	with registry-backed `Atom.getResult(apiClientRuntime)` and `Context.get(ApiClient)`.
168	Do not repeat the keepAlive construction per loader: it creates another retained
169	atom object rather than reusing the existing registry entry.
170	The one browser Promise bridge calls generated methods directly, providing the
171	registry and AbortSignal. Server loaders combine router/request signals. Native
172	client retention must survive idle navigation and React development replay;
173	final root unmount disposes outstanding work once.
174	
175	TanStack owns loader results, preload and freshness. Remove the earlier proposed
176	page/search/catalogue request atoms, resource-client replicas, success/error
177	loader envelopes and second result cache. Component-owned reactive remote reads
178	may use native ApiClient.query/mutation. Native query helpers can turn transport
179	or Schema errors into defects, so qualify recovery on the actual chosen path.
180	Retain the calculator's real local form/command state, not a parallel route cache.
181	Migrate existing `websiteCatalogueAtom` consumers to readonly root-loader data
182	or a genuinely component-owned native query; do not duplicate route results
183	in configuration atoms. Browser tools can use the same native client directly.
184	Plain successful views use native TanStack serialisation; convert only values
185	requiring an explicit checked view. Translate typed failures once to native
186	not-found/error handling with fixed safe diagnostics. Public machine envelopes
187	are existing contracts and are not removed with Website-only envelopes.
188	
189	Wrap the entire generated endpoint call in the feature's Effect timeout,
190	including headers, body consumption and decoding; retain TaxKit's named timeout
191	projection. A timeout around an unconsumed HttpClient response covers header
192	acquisition only; its transformResponse callback can also consume the body.
193	HttpApiClient/AtomHttpApi transformResponse runs after headers, so timing that
194	callback alone misses header acquisition. Bound the complete generated call.
195	A necessary two-MiB HTTP adapter must
196	preserve original status, headers, streams/cleanup and declared 4xx/5xx bodies.
197	The old bounded RPC adapter filters failed statuses and reconstructs a default
198	200 response; copying it into HTTP would break native error decoding. Keep only
199	this meaningful body policy, not custom JSON codecs or blanket Cause recovery.
200	
201	Keep existing machine RPC JSON framing/revision and per-operation receive-loop
202	ownership. The Website HTTP migration needs no NDJSON conversion or RPC package
203	removal. Preserve the no-JavaScript form, body-size/read/work limits, Markdown,
204	discovery, browser tools and public contracts through focused current tests.
205	Q9 selects `defaultPreload: "intent"`, `defaultStaleTime: 60_000` and
206	`defaultPreloadStaleTime: 60_000` for public documentation/metadata using native
207	TanStack loading. Keep explicit route exceptions for live local settings and
208	personal submission/results. Do not apply public freshness to the root's
209	no-JavaScript calculation submission merely because it travels beside catalogue
210	data. Test hover, return before expiry, return after expiry and recovery from
211	failed reads. This one-minute browser policy is separate from the CDN's seven days.
212	
213	## Seven-day public caching
214	
215	Q7 is agreed on 13 October: use native version-scoped Cloudflare cache for
216	eligible public documentation and fixed calculator metadata. The API declares
217	`yield* Cloudflare.cache({ crossVersionCache: false })` before its plan-only
218	return; Website.Vite declares `cache: { enabled: true, crossVersionCache: false }`.
219	These APIs exist in installed beta.80 and the beta.81 clone; runtime/header
220	behaviour still needs TaxKit checks. There is no owned caches.default/open/match/put
221	implementation, cache runtime or provider patch.
222	
223	For eligible public successes use browser `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0`
224	and `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, stale-if-error=0`.
225	Seven days belongs to Cloudflare; browsers recheck. TanStack freshness remains
226	separate, and cached public content can be evicted earlier. Share only responses
227	that are identical public content for the relevant checked request variant.
228	
229	Stricter headers have a purpose, not an approval role. `private`/`no-store`
230	protect personal calculation inputs/results, authenticated/session data,
231	failures, malformed settings and responses setting cookies. Keep those exclusions
232	and CDN no-store where necessary; a Cloudflare-specific public header must not
233	override a private browser header. Analytics/credential operations also remain
234	uncached. The current authored no-store declarations chiefly protect error and
235	analytics replies; no blanket no-store on successful public docs was found.
236	Public Markdown/discovery currently use a five-minute browser header. Replace
237	that public policy with the agreed browser rechecking/seven-day CDN policy for
238	eligible successes. Remove other obsolete public-read restrictions if found,
239	while retaining purposeful private/error/cookie exclusions. Use one small
240	eligibility/header decision rather than duplicated precedence or TTL parsing.
241	
242	Public GET selectors use paths/query fields, not GET bodies. Keep CORS
243	`Vary: Origin`, negotiated representation `Vary: Accept` and any qualified public
244	appearance `Vary: Cookie`. Cookie variation alone never makes personal data
245	shareable; malformed or personal variants stay private. Preserve native status,
246	media type, headers, cookies, body streams and cancellation in response adapters.
247	
248	Include authored content in both Workers' build/memo inputs without importing
249	backend code into Website, and deploy each stage's pair together. New versions
250	start separate caches; deployment activation is not atomic. During authorised
251	implementation, use consumed repeated public requests to observe HIT/Age,
252	exercise format/Origin/Accept/Cookie variants in both orders, check private/error
253	responses, and prove a Preview content-only change refreshes both JSON and HTML.
254	Restore the fixture before Production. A local cache test or binding read does
255	not establish public edge reuse, and these future checks require no new receipt
256	system. See [Cloudflare header precedence](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cdn-cache-control/)
257	for why browser and CDN restrictions must agree on private responses.
258	
259	## Strict Effect design corrections
260	
261	The deeper review uses the published 0.7.1 strict Effect skill and its service,
262	Config, error, lifetime, transport and React references, alongside the matching
263	upstream clones. Common Practice is a useful implementation reference, but some
264	of its code and copied lint rules predate those requirements. Copy its ownership
265	approach; apply the current shared rules rather than reproduce an old exception.
266	
267	A service is the checked list of operations a caller can use. A Layer is a
268	recipe that supplies an implementation and its dependencies. Declaring a Layer
269	does not start it; the app builds it for the lifetime it needs.
270	Schema checks a value's shape and meaning; Config reads settings; Scope owns
271	when resources must be released. An Alchemy Output is a resource value that
272	Alchemy resolves during deployment or local development.
273	
274	| Owner | Required design |
275	| --- | --- |
276	| Domain contracts and representations | Calculator/content owners keep the Schemas, branded identities and named expected errors. Decode external values once. Reuse whole-record checks as well as fields; encode when values leave the process or enter storage. Preserve meaningful missing/undefined distinctions with the existing Option codecs. Pure tax arithmetic and immutable mappings remain plain functions. |
277	| Public service methods | Named `Effect.fn("Service.operation")`, including test implementations. Acquire transport and fixed settings when building the service, so normal public operations need no extra service requirements. Short private pipelines stay plain functions; dependent private generators use `fnUntraced`. No generator or extra file just to wrap one step. |
278	| Static Layers | Keep owned host/backend Layers static, including the retained public RPC implementations and Website composition. Supply checked dependencies through Requirements, native Layer.succeed and checked Config. Native AtomHttpApi configuration callbacks remain native composition, not owned factories. Remove HTTP helper factories without replacing them with a replica client service. |
279	| Checked transport clients | Native HttpApiClient and AtomHttpApi endpoint methods own HTTP checking. Do not copy them into domain/client replicas. Preserve existing machine RPC clients and genuine feature/host policies with their owners. |
280	| Native API host | Build shared services once in the Worker instance, keep each request's Scope and cancellation native, and keep streams in the consumer's Scope. Do not capture a request, event tracer or request Scope in an app-wide service. No ManagedRuntime around the native Worker. |
281	| Website host | Keep the existing one server runner and one browser Atom graph. Move raw Cloudflare reads into a separate live ingress Effect; select only Website-owned keys and use native `reifyBoundConfigProvider`. Do not feed the whole environment into Config or inspect Alchemy's protected markers manually. Keep the original private binding object and its existing checked capability contract. |
282	| Frontend calls | Routes use native loader outcomes and one necessary checked view conversion; containers own commands/cancellation and leaves render readonly values. Native clients decode replies once. Import runtimes through matching environment branches, preserve root registry/initial values and inspect the real browser bundle. |
283	| Failure handling | Expected failures use the named error channel. Unexpected bugs and caller cancellation retain their identity until the host handles them. Do not convert every Cause into an unavailable result. Native HTTP mapping still owns missing-route, abort and server-failure responses. |
284	
285	Two current reply adapters need correction. The private RPC buffer in
286	`apps/api/src/worker.application.ts` catches every Cause and returns 503; the MCP
287	buffer in `apps/api/src/mcp-response.boundary.ts` preserves interruption but
288	hides other unexpected defects. Recover only the named body-read, size and
289	deadline failures those adapters own. Pass cancellation and unexpected defects
290	to native handling with a safe reporter.
291	
292	That does not mean removing every `catchCause`. Website host loaders and the
293	in-process HTTP adapter deliberately use native `HttpServerError.causeResponse`

414	## Cloudflare first, with host-independent packages
415	
416	Use Effect services and Layers to describe shared operations and supply their
417	implementations. Core, rule, calculator and transport packages must not import
418	Cloudflare, Alchemy or Bun server code, interpret trusted Cloudflare headers, or
419	run Effects themselves. The SDK's private Promise adapter is a justified public
420	library execution boundary.
421	
422	The API app owns the host adapters. Cloudflare supplies native request context,
423	private bindings, rate services and sessions. Bun supplies its HTTP server and
424	configuration through one top-level runner. Both use the same tax operations.
425	Do not add a managed Promise runtime to the native API Worker.
426	
427	Matching upstream Effect 4.0.2 supports this separation: `HttpApiBuilder` captures
428	shared services, `HttpRouter` supplies the current request scope, and
429	`BunHttpServer` supplies the abstract server. `HttpRouter.provideRequest` builds
430	its supplied Layer per request; it must not own an application-wide capacity
431	pool. Alchemy's Worker bridge builds the application once and supplies native
432	request context. Stream cleanup belongs to the current consumer; isolate
433	shutdown is not a guaranteed cleanup hook.
434	
435	Cloudflare already captures one bounded calculation service. Keep its shared
436	eight-place pool, five-second work budget and checked private identity. The pool
437	is shared within a running Worker, not across the world; Cloudflare's separate
438	native rate limit is approximate and per location. A timer cannot interrupt
439	synchronous calculation code. Q6 selects public browser access; the trusted
440	private identity and calculation limits are unchanged.
441	
442	Bun currently builds the bounded service per request, creating a fresh pool for
443	each one. Fix that at Bun application composition after the Cloudflare work.
444	Keep its current HTTP coverage and explicitly owned CORS/admission differences;
445	no Cloudflare Durable Object substitute or new Bun protocol promise is needed.

lifecycle: proposed
authority: supporting
owner: taxkit-architecture-owner
last_reviewed: 2026-10-13
